<h2 style="font-size: 1.6rem; font-weight: 700; color: #0f172a; margin-top: 2.5rem;">Anti-Reward-Hacking &amp; Physical Grounding Guarantees</h2>
<p style="color: #64748b; font-size: 0.95rem;">
  In autonomous design search, <strong>reward hacking</strong> occurs whenever an optimizer exploits simplifications in a proxy objective to report artificial gains without producing manufacturable silicon. The Grounded Workbench enforces multi-dimensional Pareto gates grounded in real EDA tools:
</p>

<div class="matrix-container">
  <table class="matrix-table">
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th style="width: 20%;">Micro-Loop</th>
        <th style="width: 25%; background: #fee2e2; color: #991b1b;">Naive / Hacked Proxy Metric</th>
        <th style="width: 25%; background: #fef3c7; color: #92400e;">Hidden Physical Penalty</th>
        <th style="width: 30%; background: #ccfbf1; color: #115e59;">Grounded Signoff Gate (Enforced)</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <td style="font-weight: 700;">Loop A: Microarchitecture</td>
        <td>Compute cycles (<i>T</i><sub>comp</sub>) or theoretical peak MACs/s</td>
        <td>DRAM interface saturation: PEs stall 78% of the time waiting for off-chip memory fills</td>
        <td style="background-color: #f0fdfa;"><strong>Joint Roofline Latency:</strong> <i>T</i><sub>effective</sub> = max(<i>T</i><sub>comp</sub>, <i>T</i><sub>dram</sub>) via <code>SCALE-Sim v3.0.0</code></td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td style="font-weight: 700;">Loop B: RTL &amp; Synthesis</td>
        <td>Target clock frequency or positive slack</td>
        <td>Circular carry propagation delay and silent arithmetic logic corruption</td>
        <td style="background-color: #f0fdfa;"><strong>Two-Key Signoff:</strong> Positive Slack (WNS &ge; 0 ps) + 1,000-vector Formal Equivalence via <code>Yosys + Icarus</code></td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td style="font-weight: 700;">Loop C: Physical Design</td>
        <td>Half-Perimeter Wirelength (HPWL) minimization</td>
        <td>Pin-escape track saturation and unroutable DRC shorts (&gt;85% track density)</td>
        <td style="background-color: #f0fdfa;"><strong>Detailed 2D RUDY Routing:</strong> Track capacity saturation &le; 85% and exactly 0 DRC shorts</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td style="font-weight: 700;">Loop D: HW/SW Co-Design</td>
        <td>Scalar arithmetic speedup or loop unrolling</td>
        <td>Register file exhaustion forcing 32,000 cycles of stack memory spilling</td>
        <td style="background-color: #f0fdfa;"><strong>End-to-End Cycle &amp; Area Accounting:</strong> ALU + Address Math + Spills + Area &le; 15,000 GE via <code>RISC-V GCC</code></td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</div>

        <h3 class="exhibit-title">500 MHz PE Accumulator Timing Closure &amp; Carry-Save Refactoring</h3>
      </div>
      <span class="text-muted font-monospace small">Yosys 0.33 &middot; Icarus Verilog &middot; 1,000 Vectors</span>

      <img src="/images/workbench/loop-b-results.png" class="exhibit-img" alt="Micro-Loop B Results Plot">
      <div class="exhibit-finding">
        <strong>Core Physical Takeaway:</strong> An ungrounded LLM (AI-Assisted) drafts a naive ripple-carry adder (`acc <= acc + in`), incurring 32 logic stages and failing timing ($WNS = -0.600$ ns at 500 MHz). An automated synthesis tool sweep (AI-Driven) optimizes cell sizing and insertion buffers, shrinking stages from 32 to 26, but still fails ($WNS = -0.072$ ns) because local optimizers cannot change arithmetic representations. The AI-Native refactoring decouples carry and sum vectors (`{c_reg, s_reg}`), reducing logic depth to a single 3:2 compressor cell (1 logic stage, 0.55 ns delay, <strong>$WNS = +1.450$ ns</strong>, verified 100% equivalent across 1,000 testbench vectors).
      </div>

        <h3 class="exhibit-title">Physical Macro Placement &amp; The Half-Perimeter Wirelength (HPWL) Paradox</h3>
      </div>
      <span class="text-muted font-monospace small">130nm Track Capacity &middot; RUDY 2D Congestion</span>
    </div>
    <div class="exhibit-body">
      <img src="/images/workbench/loop-c-results.png" class="exhibit-img" alt="Micro-Loop C Results Plot">
      <div class="exhibit-finding">
        <strong>Core Physical Takeaway:</strong> Minimizing wirelength alone (HPWL) is a dangerous surrogate metric. The AI-Driven placement packs SRAM macros tightly against the central systolic core to minimize wirelength ($HPWL = 7{,}820$ µm), but chokes the macro pin breakout corridors, exceeding 100% track capacity and creating 2 fatal DRC shorts. The AI-Native co-adaptation trades off nominal wirelength ($HPWL = 8{,}240$ µm) to rotate macro pin breakouts toward peripheral avenues and allocate dedicated $110$ µm routing channels, dropping peak congestion to <strong>34.3% with 0 DRC shorts</strong>.
      </div>

        <strong>Core Physical Takeaway:</strong> Isolated opcode generation (AI-Assisted) provides a scalar `xr_max_s32` instruction, but 71% of runtime is wasted in scalar pointer manipulation and memory loads (145,000 cycles, failing the 50k budget). Aggressive compiler loop unrolling (AI-Driven `-O3 -funroll-all-loops`) expands live ranges beyond the 32 RISC-V registers, triggering catastrophic register pressure collapse and adding <strong>32,000 cycles of stack spilling</strong>. The AI-Native solution co-designs a SIMD-4 vector datapath with auto post-increment addressing, eliminating address calculation and register spills completely (<strong>28,500 cycles, 5.1&times; speedup</strong>, 9.4k GE area).
      </div>
